start_here: Say to your AI: "Which events did my Resend account send to webhook 00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000011, and did each arrive?" It runs tool:list-webhook-events.
no_lists_because: It keeps no list of yours: it reads the events your email-sending account sent to one webhook and writes nothing.
instructions: 1. Connect your Resend account once, so its key is held in your vault under a name of yours (a key with full access). The key is never typed into the request.
2. Get the webhook's id from tool:list-resend-webhooks.

3. Say to your AI: "List the events of my Resend webhook <id>", and give the held key's name. It calls tools:run with tool tool:list-webhook-events and {"key_name": "<that name>", "webhook_id": "<id>"}.
4. Read each event's id (msg_...), type, time and status. An event whose status is failed never reached your address; tool:replay-a-webhook-event sends it again.

worked_examples.title: One event delivered, one failed
worked_examples.ask: Which events did my Resend webhook 00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000011 get, and did each arrive?
worked_examples.given: Read from tools/email-sending-domains/tool-rows.json: the row sends GET https://api.resend.com/webhooks/00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000011/events?limit=100 with your key in the Authorization header and returns Resend's reply unchanged. The events are a synthetic sample in the shape of Resend's list-events reference.

drafted_from: tools/email-sending-domains/tool-rows.json (its row) and Resend's list-events reference (https://resend.com/docs/api-reference/webhooks/list-events, read 2026-11-25)
